description: Team Exodynamics, we want to learn more about how technologies intersect with science in order to help others.
summary:
SAR-Pulse is an interactive environmental analysis platform that investigates how satellite radar can reveal seasonal surface-water changes across different wetland ecosystems. Built around NASA–ISRO NISAR L-band observations, the platform processes real synthetic aperture radar data to map water extent, estimate changes between acquisitions, and compare observations with complementary C-band radar and optical satellite references.

Across four study areas, Sylhet, Okavango, Tonlé Sap, and Atchafalaya, we investigate how radar wavelength and vegetation type influence the interpretation of environmental change. Our analysis identified notably low L-band/C-band agreement in herbaceous wetlands, raising important questions about how different radar systems observe complex environments.

SAR-Pulse combines geospatial processing, interactive maps, cross-sensor comparisons, and uncertainty diagnostics. By making satellite observations easier to explore and interpret, it demonstrates how Earth observation can support environmental research and improve understanding of seasonal wetland dynamics.
details:
What does SAR-Pulse do?

SAR-Pulse is an interactive geospatial analysis platform that investigates seasonal surface-water changes using satellite observations. Its primary data source is NASA–ISRO NISAR Level-2 Geocoded Polarimetric Covariance (GCOV) data, which provides calibrated L-band radar observations.

The platform processes satellite acquisitions through a geospatial pipeline involving data ingestion, preprocessing, spatial alignment, backscatter analysis, water classification, temporal comparison, and reference-based validation. The resulting data is presented through interactive maps, analytical visualizations, and comparison tools.

Research and findings

We processed four wetland study areas: Sylhet in Bangladesh, the Okavango Delta, Tonlé Sap in Cambodia, and the Atchafalaya Basin. Our investigation examines how radar wavelength and vegetation characteristics influence the observation of environmental change.

In Sylhet, our analysis estimated approximately 308 km² of receding open water between June 18 and October 16, 2026. We also examined the land-cover composition of emerged areas. Across our cross-sensor analysis, herbaceous wetlands showed notably low L-band/C-band agreement in Sylhet and Okavango. This suggests that radar wavelength and environmental characteristics may influence how surface changes are interpreted, although the physical cause remains unconfirmed.

Benefits and intended impact

SAR-Pulse makes complex satellite observations more accessible by combining processing outputs, interactive maps, cross-sensor comparisons, and uncertainty diagnostics. Its approach could support environmental researchers and wetland-monitoring organizations investigating seasonal water dynamics. It is a research and analysis platform, not a real-time warning system.

Technology Used

The backend and geospatial processing pipeline use Python, FastAPI, NumPy, Rasterio/GDAL, rio-tiler, h5py, earthaccess, pyogrio, and Shapely. The frontend uses TypeScript, React, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, MapLibre GL JS, and lucide-react. The application is deployed through Vercel. Additionally, we used Claude Opus 5.5 in our programming and development workflow to allow us to focus on getting our ideas onto paper rather than getting stuck on small hurdles.

Creativity and considerations

Our creative contribution is investigating wavelength-dependent radar interpretation across multiple wetland environments rather than treating satellite change detection as one universal measurement.

We considered differences in sensor wavelength, polarization, vegetation, spatial resolution, acquisition timing, reference-data quality, and classification uncertainty. We also distinguish single-date water-map validation from temporal change-detection validation and explicitly communicate the absence of field ground truth.
